raw_response:
I will do it much like I did before, because changing too much is risky and fertilizer costs real money. My land is 13.1 mu, and it is wheat-maize on the same ground, so I will plant wheat on the full 13.1 mu, then maize on the same 13.1 mu after wheat comes off. I have farmed 35 years, so I do not like to gamble with yield. Around here, if wheat is short of fertilizer, the heads stay small, and if maize is short, the ears do not fill. So I would rather spend a bit more on fertilizer than lose harvest. I will follow what works in the village: improved wheat seed, hybrid maize seed, rotary tillage because it is quicker and cheaper than deep ploughing every time, and well irrigation when the crop really needs it. For wheat, I will use more nitrogen than potash, give it about 3 irrigations if water is normal, and spray about 2 times for weeds and disease. For maize, I will use a little more nitrogen than wheat after the summer rains start, give it about 2 irrigations with the well if rain is not enough, and spray about 2 times for weeds and insects. On 13.1 mu, I still count money carefully because family also needs cash for other things, so I will not go fancy. I will do the same kind of plan across the whole field, steady and safe, aiming for a decent wheat crop first and then a full maize crop after that.
